case.title: Focus returns to the opener and moves on when a focused card leaves
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide. For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on: {Technician-A} and {Technician-B}. For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C97022 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}, both led by {Technician-A}. Neither has a shift on the Schedule, and {Technician-B} is not the technician on any of their lines. For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept 92916, with work orders S2-37664 and S2-37665.
  • For steps 14 to 16: a third technician {Technician-C}, active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on, whose last name is one word used by no other staff member or customer, and one Approved work order {Work-order-3} led by {Technician-C} for another customer {Customer-B}. For example: {Technician-C} is ZZAUTOTEST Eve E65763 and {Work-order-3} is S11582-17583.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Click once in "Search", then press Tab until a card in {Technician-A}'s column shows a blue focus ring.
  2. Press Tab.
  3. Press Enter.
  4. Press Escape.
  5. Press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  6. Press Escape.
  7. With the mouse, click "Technician" in the filter bar, tick {Technician-A} and press Escape.
  8. Click once in "Search", then press Tab until the top card in {Technician-A}'s column shows a blue focus ring.
  9. Press Tab, press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  10. In the window, choose {Technician-B} with the keyboard and confirm with the keyboard.
  11. Press Tab, press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  12. In the window, choose {Technician-B} with the keyboard and confirm with the keyboard.
  13. Press Enter.
  14. Clear "Search", make sure no filter is chosen, and type the last name of {Technician-C} in "Search" (for example E65763).
  15. Click once in "Search", press Tab until {Work-order-3}'s card shows a blue focus ring, press Tab, press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  16. In the window, choose {Technician-B} with the keyboard and confirm with the keyboard.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one of the two cards in {Technician-A}'s column has a blue focus ring.
  • Step 2: that card's "More actions" (…) button shows and has the focus ring.
  • Step 3: the "More actions" menu opens and offers "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 4: the menu closes, nothing changes, and the focus ring is back on the "More actions" button.
  • Step 5: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens.
  • Step 6: the window closes, the card still has {Technician-A} as its lead, and the focus ring is back on the "More actions" button.
  • Step 7: only {Technician-A}'s column shows, holding both {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}. Every other column is hidden.
  • Step 8: the top card in {Technician-A}'s column has the focus ring.
  • Step 9: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens for that work order.
  • Step 10: the window closes and the card leaves {Technician-A}'s column (it no longer matches the Technician filter). The focus ring moves to the other card, the one left in {Technician-A}'s column, and can be seen.
  • Step 11: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens for the last work order.
  • Step 12: the window closes and the last card leaves. The board is replaced by "No work orders match these filters", then "Try removing a filter to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button. The "Clear all filters" button has the focus ring.
  • Step 13: the filters are cleared, including the Technician filter, and the board shows the technicians' columns again. {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are both in {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 14: only {Work-order-3}'s card shows, in {Technician-C}'s column.
  • Step 15: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens for {Work-order-3}.
  • Step 16: the window closes and the card leaves. The board is replaced by “No work orders match the search "{search}".” with no button, and “When the move leaves nothing matching a search with no filters active, so the view shows the search empty state (S1-N1b), which has no button, focus moves to that empty state’s message, so the next Tab continues from there.” (PRD version 77, S11-E1)

Steps 14 to 16 added 26 Oct 2026 for PRD version 77 (26 Oct 2026), which Chris Ward wrote on SV-11582: “Please move focus to the empty state's message in that case, so the next Tab continues from there and keyboard users are never sent back to the top of the page.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 77 (26 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026

  • S11-E1 (version 77): “When the focused work order leaves the result (for example after a filter change or a reassignment), focus moves to the next row or card in the same group or column, or to that group or column header when none is left. When the move leaves nothing matching the filters, so the board or table is replaced by the “No work orders match these filters” empty state (S1-N1a), for example moving the last work order of the only technician chosen in the Technician filter, focus moves to its Clear all filters button. When the move leaves nothing matching a search with no filters active, so the view shows the search empty state (S1-N1b), which has no button, focus moves to that empty state’s message, so the next Tab continues from there.”
  • S1-N1b: “With only a search active, the empty state reads “No work orders match the search "{search}".” and shows no button.”

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, stories SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View) and SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); ticket SV-11582

  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R2: “Every control a mouse can use in Tech View and Board View is reachable with Tab and works with Enter or Space, as the design system’s menus and dialogs do: the more-actions button (which appears on keyboard focus, S3-R13), the Columns options, the x on a filter chip, and the display switcher. Technician names behind avatars show on keyboard focus, the same as on hover.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • S3-R14: “Include the lead technician action in the card’s more-actions menu: “Assign lead technician” on a work order with no lead technician, “Reassign lead technician” on one that has a lead technician.”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-R4: “The card or row more-actions menu opens the lead technician dialog, titled “Assign lead technician” or “Reassign lead technician” to match the menu item it was opened from (S3-R14).”
  • S11-R5: “Escape closes an open menu, dialog or tooltip without changing anything.”
  • S11-R6: “When a menu or dialog closes, focus returns to the control that opened it.”
  • S1-R15: “Choosing one or more shows only those technicians’ groups or columns; every other group or column, pinned ones included, is hidden.”
  • S11-E1: “When the focused work order leaves the result (for example after a filter change or a reassignment), focus moves to the next row or card in the same group or column, or to that group or column header when none is left. When the move leaves nothing matching the filters, so the board or table is replaced by the “No work orders match these filters” empty state (S1-N1a), for example moving the last work order of the only technician chosen in the Technician filter, focus moves to its Clear all filters button.”
  • S1-N1a: “With filters active, with or without a search, the empty state reads “No work orders match these filters”, then “Try removing a filter to widen your results.”, with a Clear all filters button.”
  • S1-R15a: “The Technician filter combines with every other filter and with Assigned to me: a work order shows only if it matches all of them. When nothing matches, the empty state of S1-N1a applies, and Clear all filters also clears the Technician filter.”

From: Chris Ward's answer to question 34, "WO Board and Tech View – questions for Chris Ward" (Google Sheet 1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU, row 39), answered 20 Oct 2026, read 20 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 34: “34. (b). The "No work orders match these filters" empty state shows (S1-N1a), and keyboard focus moves to its Clear all filters button. Focus going to the column header (S11-E1) still applies when a move leaves other work orders on screen. The build drops focus to the page today, so please log that as a bug against S11-E1. PRD v70.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.
